answer: Require every agent to pass a verifiable delay function before registering, like climbers queuing on a terrace below the summit: each identity costs minutes of sequential compute that cannot be parallelized, so one machine can only mint a few identities per epoch. The registry keeps each proof as a relic of work done and rejects duplicates, so an attacker wanting ten thousand fake agents must pay ten thousand sequential delays, while an honest agent pays once and reuses its identity.
